**7B.6 Research Note: Ali Khamenei in 2024**

**Overall read:** mostly **no**. I found one narrow, procedural positive signal in the nuclear-oversight channel, but the year’s stronger pattern is **blocking scrutiny, punishing journalists, blocking oversight bodies, and refusing independent investigation of abuses**. I did **not** find reliable 2024 reporting showing open investigation of Khamenei’s assets, campaign finance, conflicts of interest, or associates.

**Accepted claims**

- **Iran would not impede UN watchdog access, but only in the narrow nuclear-oversight channel** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-12-14 | https://theprint.in/world/iran-will-not-impede-iaea-access-head-of-its-atomic-organisation-says/2403254/ | Iran’s atomic chief said the country would not obstruct IAEA access and would operate within safeguards. This is the clearest limited positive signal for procedural openness, but it is narrow, late, and about nuclear verification rather than independent inquiry into Khamenei’s conduct, assets, or associates. | **QIDs:** 7B.6, 7B.1, 7B.2

- **IAEA talks stayed open after Grossi’s visit** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-07 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaeas-grossi-seeks-deal-with-iran-on-nuclear-steps-soon-3425312 | Reuters reported that talks would continue and a package of measures should be reached soon. This is only indirect evidence of tolerance for technical inspection, not evidence that Khamenei welcomed independent scrutiny of his own decisions or finances. | **QIDs:** 7B.6

- **Iran barred many senior IAEA enrichment experts, weakening independent verification** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-05 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaea-board-passes-resolution-against-iran-on-cooperation-inspectors-3472087 | The IAEA Board called on Iran to reverse its barring of inspectors after Iran removed many experienced inspectors. That is strong evidence against tolerance for independent investigation in a sensitive domain. | **QIDs:** 7B.6, 7B.1, 7B.2

- **Late-year IAEA cooperation remained contested, not fully open** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-11-21 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaea-board-passes-iran-resolution-as-west-pushes-tehran-towards-talks-3736230 | The Board again pressed Iran to improve cooperation and provide a comprehensive report. This reinforces that independent scrutiny remained incomplete and conditional rather than genuinely tolerated. | **QIDs:** 7B.6

- **Journalists were still punished for reporting on sensitive abuses** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-10-13 | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/iran-reduces-sentence-of-jailed-journalists-after-clearing-them-of-collaborating-with-us-3660786 | Reuters reported a partial sentence reduction for two journalists, but they still remained punished for reporting on Amini’s death. This is weak corrective behavior, not real tolerance for independent investigation. | **QIDs:** 7B.6, 7B.2

- **Iran’s judiciary kept criminalizing investigative reporting** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-24 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/24/journalists-ordered-serve-five-years-prison-iran | HRW said journalists were ordered to serve prison terms for reporting on Amini’s death and that the case was framed as propaganda against the state. This is direct evidence against tolerance for independent reporting or inquiry. | **QIDs:** 7B.6, 7B.2

- **No effective independent investigations into killings, torture, sexual violence, or disappearances** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-11 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/ | Amnesty said there were no effective, impartial, or independent criminal investigations and that families seeking truth faced harassment and arbitrary detention. This is strong evidence that the system did not tolerate independent investigation of state conduct. | **QIDs:** 7B.6, 7B.2

- **Transparency remained extremely limited, with information suppressed and institutions above scrutiny** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/iran/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says information is suppressed or manipulated, transparency is extremely limited, and powerful institutions remain above scrutiny. This is strong background evidence against open investigation of finances, conflicts, and concealed decisions. | **QIDs:** 7B.6, 7B.4, 7B.3

- **Even nominal oversight of the supreme leader stayed tightly controlled** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-01-24 | https://theprint.in/world/iran-bans-ex-president-rouhani-from-running-for-elite-assembly/1937211/ | The Guardian Council barred Hassan Rouhani from the Assembly of Experts, the body that can appoint or dismiss the supreme leader. That is direct evidence against tolerating an independent mechanism that could investigate or constrain Khamenei. | **QIDs:** 7B.6, 7B.3

- **The succession-linked oversight body was structurally subordinated to Khamenei’s camp** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-02-29 | https://theprint.in/world/factbox-key-facts-about-irans-elections-on-friday/1983652/ | Reuters explained that Assembly of Experts candidates must pass Guardian Council vetting. That means the body that might investigate or remove the supreme leader was not independent in practice. | **QIDs:** 7B.6, 7B.3

**Search gap**

I did **not** find reliable 2024 reporting showing:
- public asset disclosure by Khamenei,
- independent audits of his finances or campaign-related resources,
- investigations into his close associates by autonomous bodies,
- or any meaningful tolerance for probing concealed official decisions outside the narrow nuclear-IAEA channel.

The available evidence is mostly **negative background** plus one **limited procedural exception** for nuclear inspections.
